title: Mini resume + prefetch protocol: SDK scrapbook
body:
Purpose

This is a lightweight, pragmatic proposal-scrapbook for an SDK-oriented 'mini resume + prefetch' protocol targeted at latency-sensitive clients (mobile/web SDKs) using the Hosted API streaming surface and tool-calling. Aim: reduce perceived cold-start latency for tool-heavy flows, enable resumable partial responses, and make structured outputs easier to reconcile on client rehydrate. This is intentionally informal — notes, sketches, and tradeoffs for engineering/product to iterate from.

Problems we see in the field
- Mobile/embedded clients observe long tail waiting while server warms tool runtimes or fetches remote resources for tool calls.
- Network interruptions lead to lost partial outputs or duplicated tool invocations when clients retry.
- Structured output (JSON/records) is fragile when partial frames are dropped: clients either get invalid JSON or must re-run large prompts to reconstruct state.
- SDK ergonomics: client code prefers small, composable primitives rather than full-session semantics. We should avoid forcing heavy session storage.

High level idea
- Introduce a compact client-visible 'prefetch manifest' baked into request metadata. The manifest hints the runtime about toollets, external resource URIs, and key tokens (e.g., entity ids) that the server can warm/opportunistically fetch before progressing the main generation path.
- Allow the server to emit micro-checkpoints (microframes) containing structured deltas and an idempotency token for tool invocations (toollet-lease). Clients can resume from the latest acknowledged microframe instead of re-running entire prompt.
- Keep protocol minimal: optional headers + small sequence numbers + delta JSON frames. SDK exposes a few helpers: applyDelta(), resumeFromCheckpoint(), prefetchHints().

Goals
- Improve median and P95 perceived latency for flows that trigger tool calls by enabling server-side prewarm of toollets based on client hints.
- Make retries idempotent: when a client reconnects, it can indicate the last microframe it received; server will avoid re-executing any tool invocation with a valid lease id.
- Offer structured partial updates so clients can update UI progressively without needing to parse incomplete JSON.
- Keep SDK surface tiny and explicit; favor developer control over magic.

Non-goals
- This is not a full-blown session persistence layer for long lived multimodal experiences.
- Not a replacement for existing canary/fallback routing at infra level.

Protocol sketch (client -> hosted API)
- Request metadata: X-RW-Prefetch-Manifest: base64(JSON) where JSON = {"tools": ["web-search","run-query"], "uris": ["/user/123/profile"], "stitch_key": "u123-snap2"}
- Optional: X-RW-Resume-From: microframe_seq (int) — indicates highest microframe client persisted.
- Optional: X-RW-Client-Hints: {"bandwidth":"low","latency_budget_ms":150} (used by runtime to choose prefetch aggressiveness).

Server semantics (runtime)
- On receipt, runtime evaluates manifest and: 1) if tool warm cache suggests miss, enqueue prefetch actions to tool pool; 2) respond to first bytes as soon as an initial outline token is ready but delay heavy function calls until prefetch completes if client hinted high latency sensitivity.
- Emit microframes over streaming channel with small structured envelope types: META (progress), DELTA (structured partial), TOOL_INVOCATION (tool call result paired with lease id), CHECKPOINT (sequence id + safe cursor).

Microframe envelope examples (text streaming lines)
- {"t":"META","s":1,"msg":"outline ready"}
- {"t":"DELTA","s":2,"body":{"summary":"first pass"}}
- {"t":"TOOL_INV","s":3,"lease":"tl-6a3f","tool":"web-search","result":{"hits": [...]}}
- {"t":"CHECKPOINT","s":4,"cursor":"cptr-4","safe_resume":true}

Key ergonomics for SDKs
- Minimal API surface: RequestBuilder.prefetchHints(manifest), StreamReader.onDelta(callback), StreamReader.getLastCheckpoint(), ResumeController.resumeFromCheckpoint(id).
- Provide a small local cache for 'lease ids' and 'last_checkpoint_seq' persisted for short TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) to enable quick resume when network blips occur. Not intended as long-term durable storage.
- Helper to reconcile structured DELTA frames into a canonical object (applyDelta(base, delta)). Provide a default shallow-merge and allow custom merge hooks for client types.

Tool idempotency and leases
- Each server-initiated tool invocation includes a stable lease id. If client reconnects advertising last acknowledged seq >= seq_of_tool_invocation, runtime treats tool invocation as already consumed and will not re-run the underlying call.
- Lease lifetime: short (e.g., 10 minutes). Must be coordinated with Dedicated/Private infra to ensure cross-replica semantics if necessary.

Failure and fallback modes
- If client cannot persist checkpoint, default to full-request retry but runtime will attempt cheap duplication avoidance using request fingerprint and tool call signatures. Not guaranteed.
- If prefetch misses and runtime chooses not to stall, server emits a progressive DELAY metadata so client can show spinner or degrade to a simpler answer.

Security and privacy considerations
- Prefetch manifest may contain customer-specific URIs or identifiers. Runtime must treat manifests as sensitive and adhere to the same data isolation rules as the request body. Do not log raw manifest in plaintext in high-retention telemetry.
- Tool-lease tokens are short lived and should not be usable to fetch results from APIs directly; they are only server-side coordination handles.

Observability / instrumentation to add
- Metrics: manifest_hit_rate, avg_prefetch_latency_ms, microframe_gap_ms, discarded_resumes, lease_reuse_rate.
- Tracing: surface trace spans for prefetch actions, toollet-warm spans, and resume reconciliation. Correlate with request id and checkpoint seq.

Migration path and rollout plan (MVP -> beta -> GA)
- MVP (experiment): server accepts prefetch manifest but treats it as advisory. SDK surface in internal beta only; telemetry on manifest usage and improvement to latency.
- Beta: enable server prefetch actively for clients on opt-in, implement lease id behavior, expose client SDK helpers, gradually roll to power users.
- GA: on by default with opt-out flag for privacy-sensitive customers and full docs for enterprise private deployment specifics.

Open engineering questions (short list)
- How to coordinate lease semantics across multi-replica Dedicated clusters? Suggest central lease store or include stable request fingerprint in lease validation.
- How big should microframes be? We want them compact to avoid extra RTTs, but too small increases overhead. Default: max 2KB per DELTA.
- How do we surface structured validation failures to SDKs? Proposal: CHECKPOINT includes optional validation hash; client can request re-sync if mismatch.

Sample SDK usage snippet (pseudo)
- builder.prefetchHints({tools:["finance-lookup"],uris:["/acct/xyz"],stitch_key:"acct-xyz-s1"})
- stream = client.streamWithResume(builder)
- stream.onDelta(d => ui.applyDelta(d))
- stream.onCheckpoint(c => localStore.save({seq:c.s, leaseIds:c.lease_ids}))
- on reconnect: client.resumeFromCheckpoint(localStore.lastSeq)

Next steps / TODOs
- Spike: runtime prefetch worker prototype + telemetry hook (2 weeks).
- SDK: add resume helpers to JS/Swift/Android, small local TTL cache (3 weeks).
- Product: run two small pilot integrations (notes app + search assistant) and collect latency/duplicate-invocation data.
- Security: review manifest logging policy and enterprise opt-out controls.

Notes to self
- This doc is intentionally messy. Pull out a clean PRD if pilot data shows promise. Include small sample traces in follow-up.

References and inspirations
- Internal: incremental-snapshot-resume-protocol, session-fragmentation-client-replay notes (see linked artifacts).
notes: Prefer simple explicit SDK API over magic background resume
Make prefetch manifest optional and privacy-aware
